about: A point is a place where origins can coincide: its state is the set of origins that touched it, with the span each
one holds. "Has a second origin", "where do they disagree" and "what turned" are reads of that set at the point,
never a join over a key somebody chose: the coordinate is the key (L00), and an encounter is two origins in one
It got its own file because reconciliation is an industry: with relations stored and coincidence searched afterwards,
asking whether two origins saw one thing costs a pass over everything; here it costs reading one set.

cases.name: one origin is potential, and grey
the same origin twice is still one origin
two origins that meet are an encounter, and what stands is the meet
two origins that do not meet split the point, and the pair is named
a third origin does not hide the pair that splits
no origin at all is grey

turned.note: what travels between two readings is which points changed colour, never the structure (L13)

coverage.criterion: no origin, one origin, one origin twice, two that meet, two that split, and a third that must not hide the split
coverage.why: one scale; the pair named by a split is the first pair the witness search finds, and only that order is pinned
